code:
require 'net/http'
require 'uri'
require 'rss'
require 'time'

# fetch_feed method implementation for rss_feed_fetcher
# Active contract: fetch and parse RSS/Atom feeds, return structured items

url = kwargs[:url] || args.first

unless url
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "missing_parameter",
    error_message: "URL parameter is required",
    retriable: false
  )
  return result
end

begin
  uri = URI.parse(url)
  
  # Follow redirects manually (302 caused previous failure)
  redirect_limit = 5
  response = nil
  current_uri = uri
  
  redirect_limit.times do
    http = Net::HTTP.new(current_uri.host, current_uri.port)
    http.use_ssl = (current_uri.scheme == 'https')
    http.open_timeout = 10
    http.read_timeout = 10
    
    request = Net::HTTP::Get.new(current_uri.request_uri)
    request['User-Agent'] = 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; RSS Feed Fetcher)'
    
    response = http.request(request)
    
    case response
    when Net::HTTPSuccess
      break
    when Net::HTTPRedirection
      location = response['location']
      current_uri = URI.parse(location)
    else
      result = Agent::Outcome.error(
        error_type: "http_error",
        error_message: "HTTP request failed with status #{response.code}: #{response.message}",
        retriable: true
      )
      return result
    end
  end
  
  unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPSuccess)
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "http_error",
      error_message: "Too many redirects or final response was not successful",
      retriable: true
    )
    return result
  end
  
  feed_content = response.body
  fetched_at = Time.now.utc.iso8601
  
  # Parse RSS/Atom feed
  feed = RSS::Parser.parse(feed_content, false)
  
  unless feed
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "parse_error",
      error_message: "Failed to parse RSS/Atom feed",
      retriable: false
    )
    return result
  end
  
  # Extract items
  items = []
  
  if feed.respond_to?(:items)
    feed.items.each do |item|
      items << {
        title: item.title.to_s,
        link: item.link.to_s,
        published: (item.pubDate || item.date || item.dc_date)&.iso8601 || "",
        description: (item.description.to_s rescue "")
      }
    end
  elsif feed.respond_to?(:entries)
    feed.entries.each do |entry|
      items << {
        title: entry.title.content.to_s,
        link: (entry.link.href rescue entry.link.to_s),
        published: (entry.published || entry.updated)&.iso8601 || "",
        description: (entry.summary&.content || entry.content&.content || "").to_s
      }
    end
  end
  
  # Return structured result with provenance
  result = Agent::Outcome.ok(
    items: items,
    source_url: url,
    fetched_at: fetched_at,
    provenance: {
      sources: [
        {
          uri: url,
          fetched_at: fetched_at,
          retrieval_tool: "rss_feed_fetcher",
          retrieval_mode: "live"
        }
      ]
    }
  )
  
rescue URI::InvalidURIError => e
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "invalid_url",
    error_message: "Invalid URL: #{e.message}",
    retriable: false
  )
rescue RSS::Error => e
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "parse_error",
    error_message: "RSS parse error: #{e.message}",
    retriable: false
  )
rescue StandardError => e
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "fetch_error",
    error_message: "Failed to fetch feed: #{e.class} - #{e.message}",
    retriable: true
  )
end

require 'net/http'
require 'uri'
require 'rss'
require 'time'

# fetch_feed method implementation for rss_feed_fetcher
# Active contract: fetch and parse RSS/Atom feeds, return structured items

url = kwargs[:url] || args.first

unless url
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "missing_parameter",
    error_message: "URL parameter is required",
    retriable: false
  )
  return result
end

begin
  uri = URI.parse(url)
  
  # Follow redirects manually (302 caused previous failure)
  redirect_limit = 5
  response = nil
  current_uri = uri
  
  redirect_limit.times do
    http = Net::HTTP.new(current_uri.host, current_uri.port)
    http.use_ssl = (current_uri.scheme == 'https')
    http.open_timeout = 10
    http.read_timeout = 10
    
    request = Net::HTTP::Get.new(current_uri.request_uri)
    request['User-Agent'] = 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; RSS Feed Fetcher)'
    
    response = http.request(request)
    
    case response
    when Net::HTTPSuccess
      break
    when Net::HTTPRedirection
      location = response['location']
      current_uri = URI.parse(location)
    else
      result = Agent::Outcome.error(
        error_type: "http_error",
        error_message: "HTTP request failed with status #{response.code}: #{response.message}",
        retriable: true
      )
      return result
    end
  end
  
  unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPSuccess)
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "http_error",
      error_message: "Too many redirects or final response was not successful",
      retriable: true
    )
    return result
  end
  
  feed_content = response.body
  fetched_at = Time.now.utc.iso8601
  
  # Parse RSS/Atom feed
  feed = RSS::Parser.parse(feed_content, false)
  
  unless feed
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "parse_error",
      error_message: "Failed to parse RSS/Atom feed",
      retriable: false
    )
    return result
  end
  
  # Extract items
  items = []
  
  if feed.respond_to?(:items)
    feed.items.each do |item|
      items << {
        title: item.title.to_s,
        link: item.link.to_s,
        published: (item.pubDate || item.date || item.dc_date)&.iso8601 || "",
        description: (item.description.to_s rescue "")
      }
    end
  elsif feed.respond_to?(:entries)
    feed.entries.each do |entry|
      items << {
        title: entry.title.content.to_s,
        link: (entry.link.href rescue entry.link.to_s),
        published: (entry.published || entry.updated)&.iso8601 || "",
        description: (entry.summary&.content || entry.content&.content || "").to_s
      }
    end
  end
  
  # Return structured result with provenance
  result = Agent::Outcome.ok(
    items: items,
    source_url: url,
    fetched_at: fetched_at,
    provenance: {
      sources: [
        {
          uri: url,
          fetched_at: fetched_at,
          retrieval_tool: "rss_feed_fetcher",
          retrieval_mode: "live"
        }
      ]
    }
  )
  
rescue URI::InvalidURIError => e
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "invalid_url",
    error_message: "Invalid URL: #{e.message}",
    retriable: false
  )
rescue RSS::Error => e
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "parse_error",
    error_message: "RSS parse error: #{e.message}",
    retriable: false
  )
rescue StandardError => e
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "fetch_error",
    error_message: "Failed to fetch feed: #{e.class} - #{e.message}",
    retriable: true
  )
end

require 'net/http'
require 'uri'
require 'rss'
require 'time'

# fetch_feed method implementation for rss_feed_fetcher
# Active contract: fetch and parse RSS/Atom feeds, return structured items

url = kwargs[:url] || args.first

unless url
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "missing_parameter",
    error_message: "URL parameter is required",
    retriable: false
  )
  return result
end

begin
  uri = URI.parse(url)
  
  # Follow redirects manually (302 caused previous failure)
  redirect_limit = 5
  response = nil
  current_uri = uri
  
  redirect_limit.times do
    http = Net::HTTP.new(current_uri.host, current_uri.port)
    http.use_ssl = (current_uri.scheme == 'https')
    http.open_timeout = 10
    http.read_timeout = 10
    
    request = Net::HTTP::Get.new(current_uri.request_uri)
    request['User-Agent'] = 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; RSS Feed Fetcher)'
    
    response = http.request(request)
    
    case response
    when Net::HTTPSuccess
      break
    when Net::HTTPRedirection
      location = response['location']
      current_uri = URI.parse(location)
    else
      result = Agent::Outcome.error(
        error_type: "http_error",
        error_message: "HTTP request failed with status #{response.code}: #{response.message}",
        retriable: true
      )
      return result
    end
  end
  
  unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPSuccess)
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "http_error",
      error_message: "Too many redirects or final response was not successful",
      retriable: true
    )
    return result
  end
  
  feed_content = response.body
  fetched_at = Time.now.utc.iso8601
  
  # Parse RSS/Atom feed
  feed = RSS::Parser.parse(feed_content, false)
  
  unless feed
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "parse_error",
      error_message: "Failed to parse RSS/Atom feed",
      retriable: false
    )
    return result
  end
  
  # Extract items
  items = []
  
  if feed.respond_to?(:items)
    feed.items.each do |item|
      items << {
        title: item.title.to_s,
        link: item.link.to_s,
        published: (item.pubDate || item.date || item.dc_date)&.iso8601 || "",
        description: (item.description.to_s rescue "")
      }
    end
  elsif feed.respond_to?(:entries)
    feed.entries.each do |entry|
      items << {
        title: entry.title.content.to_s,
        link: (entry.link.href rescue entry.link.to_s),
        published: (entry.published || entry.updated)&.iso8601 || "",
        description: (entry.summary&.content || entry.content&.content || "").to_s
      }
    end
  end
  
  # Return structured result with provenance
  result = Agent::Outcome.ok(
    items: items,
    source_url: url,
    fetched_at: fetched_at,
    provenance: {
      sources: [
        {
          uri: url,
          fetched_at: fetched_at,
          retrieval_tool: "rss_feed_fetcher",
          retrieval_mode: "live"
        }
      ]
    }
  )
  
rescue URI::InvalidURIError => e
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "invalid_url",
    error_message: "Invalid URL: #{e.message}",
    retriable: false
  )
rescue RSS::Error => e
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "parse_error",
    error_message: "RSS parse error: #{e.message}",
    retriable: false
  )
rescue StandardError => e
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "fetch_error",
    error_message: "Failed to fetch feed: #{e.class} - #{e.message}",
    retriable: true
  )
end

require 'rss'
require 'time'

# Active contract: parse RSS/Atom feeds into structured items
# Deliverable: {items: [...]} where each item has title, link, published
# Method invoked: parse(feed_string: "")

feed_string = kwargs[:feed_string] || ""

# Handle empty input case
if feed_string.nil? || feed_string.strip.empty?
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "invalid_input",
    error_message: "feed_string is empty or nil; cannot parse RSS/Atom feed",
    retriable: false,
    tool_role: "rss_parser",
    method_name: "parse"
  )
else
  begin
    # Parse the RSS/Atom feed using Ruby's built-in RSS library
    rss = RSS::Parser.parse(feed_string, false)
    
    items = []
    
    # Handle RSS 2.0 / RSS 1.0 feeds
    if rss.respond_to?(:items) && rss.items
      rss.items.each do |item|
        items << {
          title: item.title&.content || item.title.to_s,
          link: item.link&.href || item.link.to_s,
          published: item.pubDate || item.date || item.dc_date,
          description: item.description&.content || item.description.to_s
        }
      end
    # Handle Atom feeds
    elsif rss.respond_to?(:entries) && rss.entries
      rss.entries.each do |entry|
        items << {
          title: entry.title&.content || entry.title.to_s,
          link: entry.link&.href || entry.links&.first&.href.to_s,
          published: entry.published&.content || entry.updated&.content || entry.published || entry.updated,
          description: entry.summary&.content || entry.content&.content || ""
        }
      end
    end
    
    result = Agent::Outcome.ok(
      value: { items: items },
      tool_role: "rss_parser",
      method_name: "parse"
    )
    
  rescue RSS::NotWellFormedError, RSS::InvalidRSSError => e
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "parse_error",
      error_message: "Failed to parse RSS/Atom feed: #{e.message}",
      retriable: false,
      tool_role: "rss_parser",
      method_name: "parse"
    )
  rescue => e
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "unexpected_error",
      error_message: "Unexpected error parsing feed: #{e.class} - #{e.message}",
      retriable: false,
      tool_role: "rss_parser",
      method_name: "parse"
    )
  end
end

require 'net/http'
require 'uri'
require 'time'

# Active contract: fetch content from any URL via HTTP
# Deliverable: { status:, body:, url: }
# Method invoked: fetch_url with url: "https://news.google.com/rss"

url_string = kwargs[:url] || args.first
raise ArgumentError, "URL is required" unless url_string

uri = URI.parse(url_string)

begin
  response = Net::HTTP.start(uri.host, uri.port, use_ssl: uri.scheme == 'https', 
                              open_timeout: 10, read_timeout: 30) do |http|
    request = Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri.request_uri)
    request['User-Agent'] = 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; AgentFetcher/1.0)'
    http.request(request)
  end
  
  # Contract deliverable: return object with status, body, and url keys
  fetch_result = {
    status: response.code.to_i,
    body: response.body,
    url: url_string
  }
  
  # Provenance envelope for external-data success
  result = Agent::Outcome.ok(
    value: fetch_result,
    provenance: {
      sources: [{
        uri: url_string,
        fetched_at: Time.now.utc.iso8601,
        retrieval_tool: "web_fetcher",
        retrieval_mode: "live"
      }]
    }
  )
  
rescue StandardError => e
  # Failure policy: return_error
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "http_fetch_failed",
    error_message: "Failed to fetch #{url_string}: #{e.class} - #{e.message}",
    retriable: true,
    tool_role: "web_fetcher",
    method_name: "fetch_url"
  )
end

## Who You Are
You are a Tool: a delegated Ruby agent called 'web_fetcher'.
You generate Ruby code that runs in an execution sandbox.
Your code's return value (via `result` or `return`) becomes an Outcome delivered to your parent caller.
Your purpose: execute delegated contract work clearly and efficiently.
Default posture: Do/Shape. Forge only when the active contract implies a reusable interface.
## Your Environment
What you have:
- `context` is working memory.
- `context[:tools]` is the tool registry metadata.
- `context[:conversation_history]` is prior structured call history.
- `content(ref)` retrieves stored payload for `outcome_summary.content_ref`; returns `nil` if missing/evicted.
- If a role profile is active, it defines continuity constraints for sibling methods.
- Identity context: you are this role. If the registry contains your role name, that entry refers to you.
- Do NOT materialize yourself with `tool("same_role_name")` or `delegate("same_role_name", ...)`; implement directly.

Call depth:
- You are at depth 1 (delegated tool execution).
- Focus on contract execution, not speculative capability expansion.

How delegation works:
- `tool("name")` materializes an existing tool from the registry.
- Any further delegation must stay within runtime capability boundaries.
- delegation does NOT grant new capabilities.

How outcomes work:
- Dynamic call return values are wrapped as an Outcome object.
- Prefer `Agent::Outcome.ok(...)` and `Agent::Outcome.error(...)`.


## How You Think (strict order)
- You are a Tool executing delegated work: verify whether you can fulfill the task directly with current capabilities.
- Check `context[:tools]` first before creating anything new.
- `<known_tools>` is a non-exhaustive preview of the same registry metadata.
- Registry entries are metadata only; invoke tools via `tool("tool_name")` or explicit `delegate(...)`.
- If capability is missing, prefer local Shape or typed error; Forge only when the active contract clearly implies a reusable interface.

## Your Stances

## Runtime Hard Constraints
Rule Priority Order (highest first):
1. Output Format Contract (MUST)
2. Capability and Side-Effect Boundaries (MUST)
3. Tool Design Quality and Delegation Discipline (SHOULD, unless it conflicts with 1 or 2)

Output Format Contract:
- Always respond with valid GeneratedProgram payload via the execute_code tool.
- The payload MUST include `code` and MAY include `dependencies`.
- Set `result` or use `return` to produce the raw domain value (runtime wraps it in Outcome).
- Avoid `redo` unless in a clearly bounded loop; unbounded `redo` can cause non-terminating execution.

Capability and Side-Effect Boundaries:
- Side-effect integrity first: do NOT claim timers/reminders/notifications/background jobs are set unless code actually schedules them.
- Be truthful and capability-accurate; never claim an action occurred unless this code actually performed it.
- Writing to context is internal memory only, not an external side effect.
- State-key continuity rule:
    1. If context already has a key for the same semantic state, reuse that key.
    2. If no scalar accumulator key exists yet, default to `context[:value]`.
    3. Do not create parallel scalar aliases (for example `:memory`, `:accumulator`, `:calculator_value`) for the same state unless explicitly required.
    4. Setter/readback coherence: if caller sets `obj.foo = x`, prefer `context[:foo]` for that semantic state.
- `context[:tools]` entries are metadata; query them for capability-fit and materialize tools via `tool(...)`/`delegate(...)`.
- `context[:conversation_history]` is structured call history; for source follow-ups, read it first and cite concrete refs when available.
- Never infer or fabricate provenance if history refs are missing; return explicit unknown/missing-source response.
- Outcome constructors available: Agent::Outcome.ok(...), Agent::Outcome.error(...), Agent::Outcome.call(value=nil, ...).
- Prefer Agent::Outcome.ok/error as canonical forms; Agent::Outcome.call is a tolerant success alias.
- Outcome API idioms: use `outcome.ok?` / `outcome.error?` for branching, then `outcome.value` or `outcome.error_message`. (`success?`/`failure?` are tolerated aliases.)
- For tool composition, preserve contract shapes (for example, pass RSS parser raw feed string, not fetch envelope Hash).
- When consuming tool output hashes, handle both symbol and string keys unless you explicitly normalized keys.
- External-data success invariant: if code fetches/parses remote data and returns success, include provenance envelope.
- Provenance envelope shape (tolerant key types): `provenance: { sources: [{ uri:, fetched_at:, retrieval_tool:, retrieval_mode: ("live"|"cached"|"fixture") }] }`.
- delegation does NOT grant new capabilities; child tools inherit the same runtime/tooling limits.
- Do NOT delegate recursively to bypass unavailable capabilities; return typed non-retriable error instead.
- If output is structurally valid but not useful for caller intent, return `Agent::Outcome.error(error_type: "low_utility", ...)`.
- Guidance-only prose where concrete items were requested is `low_utility`, not success.
- If request crosses this Tool's boundary, return `Agent::Outcome.error(error_type: "wrong_tool_boundary", ...)`.
- Compare active `intent_signature` with Tool purpose/capabilities; on mismatch, prefer `wrong_tool_boundary`.
- If non-stdlib gems are required, declare minimal `dependencies`; keep outputs/context JSON-serializable.

Tool Design Quality and Delegation Discipline:
- Infer what methods and behaviors are natural for role 'web_fetcher'.
- Method names should be intuitive verbs or queries a caller would expect for this role.
- Write clean, focused code that fulfills the active intent/contract.
- Initialize local accumulators before appending (for example `lines = []`) before calling `<<`/`push`.
- Parameterize inputs when it improves clarity and reuse.
- Do NOT over-generalize into frameworks or speculative abstractions.
- Do NOT mutate Agent/Tool objects with metaprogramming (for example `define_singleton_method`); express behavior through normal generated methods and tool/delegate invocation paths.
- Depth 1 is execution-first: prefer direct implementation and local shaping.
- Do NOT delegate if the task is a simple computation/string operation or can be done in fewer than 10 lines.
- Forge only when active contract/deliverable clearly implies a reusable interface.
- If blocked by unavailable capability, return typed error outcome instead of pushing delegation deeper.

require 'rss'
require 'time'

# Active contract: parse RSS/Atom feeds into structured items
# Deliverable: {items: [...]} where each item has title, link, published
# Method invoked: parse(feed_string: "")

feed_string = kwargs[:feed_string] || ""

# Handle empty input case
if feed_string.nil? || feed_string.strip.empty?
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "invalid_input",
    error_message: "feed_string is empty or nil; cannot parse RSS/Atom feed",
    retriable: false,
    tool_role: "rss_parser",
    method_name: "parse"
  )
else
  begin
    # Parse the RSS/Atom feed using Ruby's built-in RSS library
    rss = RSS::Parser.parse(feed_string, false)
    
    items = []
    
    # Handle RSS 2.0 / RSS 1.0 feeds
    if rss.respond_to?(:items) && rss.items
      rss.items.each do |item|
        # Fix: item.title and item.description are already strings in RSS 2.0
        # Only call .content if the object responds to it
        title_val = if item.title.respond_to?(:content)
                      item.title.content
                    else
                      item.title.to_s
                    end
        
        link_val = if item.link.respond_to?(:href)
                     item.link.href
                   else
                     item.link.to_s
                   end
        
        desc_val = if item.description.respond_to?(:content)
                     item.description.content
                   else
                     item.description.to_s
                   end
        
        items << {
          title: title_val,
          link: link_val,
          published: item.pubDate || item.date || item.dc_date,
          description: desc_val
        }
      end
    # Handle Atom feeds
    elsif rss.respond_to?(:entries) && rss.entries
      rss.entries.each do |entry|
        title_val = if entry.title.respond_to?(:content)
                      entry.title.content
                    else
                      entry.title.to_s
                    end
        
        link_val = if entry.link.respond_to?(:href)
                     entry.link.href
                   elsif entry.links && entry.links.first
                     entry.links.first.href.to_s
                   else
                     ""
                   end
        
        summary_val = if entry.summary && entry.summary.respond_to?(:content)
                        entry.summary.content
                      elsif entry.content && entry.content.respond_to?(:content)
                        entry.content.content
                      else
                        ""
                      end
        
        pub_val = if entry.published && entry.published.respond_to?(:content)
                    entry.published.content
                  elsif entry.updated && entry.updated.respond_to?(:content)
                    entry.updated.content
                  else
                    entry.published || entry.updated
                  end
        
        items << {
          title: title_val,
          link: link_val,
          published: pub_val,
          description: summary_val
        }
      end
    end
    
    result = Agent::Outcome.ok(
      value: { items: items },
      tool_role: "rss_parser",
      method_name: "parse"
    )
    
  rescue RSS::NotWellFormedError, RSS::InvalidRSSError => e
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "parse_error",
      error_message: "Failed to parse RSS/Atom feed: #{e.message}",
      retriable: false,
      tool_role: "rss_parser",
      method_name: "parse"
    )

require 'net/http'
require 'uri'
require 'time'

# Active contract: fetch content from any URL via HTTP
# Deliverable: { status:, body:, url: }
# Method invoked: fetch_url with url: "https://news.google.com/rss"

url_string = kwargs[:url] || args.first
raise ArgumentError, "URL is required" unless url_string

uri = URI.parse(url_string)

begin
  response = Net::HTTP.start(uri.host, uri.port, use_ssl: uri.scheme == 'https', 
                              open_timeout: 10, read_timeout: 30) do |http|
    request = Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri.request_uri)
    request['User-Agent'] = 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; AgentFetcher/1.0)'
    http.request(request)
  end
  
  # Contract deliverable: return object with status, body, and url keys
  fetch_result = {
    status: response.code.to_i,
    body: response.body,
    url: url_string
  }
  
  # Provenance envelope for external-data success
  result = Agent::Outcome.ok(
    value: fetch_result,
    provenance: {
      sources: [{
        uri: url_string,
        fetched_at: Time.now.utc.iso8601,
        retrieval_tool: "web_fetcher",
        retrieval_mode: "live"
      }]
    }
  )
  
rescue StandardError => e
  # Failure policy: return_error
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "http_fetch_failed",
    error_message: "Failed to fetch #{url_string}: #{e.class} - #{e.message}",
    retriable: true,
    tool_role: "web_fetcher",
    method_name: "fetch_url"
  )
end

## Who You Are
You are a Tool: a delegated Ruby agent called 'web_fetcher'.
You generate Ruby code that runs in an execution sandbox.
Your code's return value (via `result` or `return`) becomes an Outcome delivered to your parent caller.
Your purpose: execute delegated contract work clearly and efficiently.
Default posture: Do/Shape. Forge only when the active contract implies a reusable interface.
## Your Environment
What you have:
- `context` is working memory.
- `context[:tools]` is the tool registry metadata.
- `context[:conversation_history]` is prior structured call history.

- If a role profile is active, it defines continuity constraints for sibling methods.
- Identity context: you are this role. If the registry contains your role name, that entry refers to you.

Call depth:
- You are at depth 1 (delegated tool execution).
- Focus on contract execution, not speculative capability expansion.

How delegation works:
- `tool("name")` materializes an existing tool from the registry.
- Any further delegation must stay within runtime capability boundaries.
- delegation does NOT grant new capabilities.

How outcomes work:
- Dynamic call return values are wrapped as an Outcome object.
- Prefer `Agent::Outcome.ok(...)` and `Agent::Outcome.error(...)`.


## How You Think (strict order)
- You are a Tool executing delegated work: verify whether you can fulfill the task directly with current capabilities.
- Check `context[:tools]` first before creating anything new.
- `<known_tools>` is a non-exhaustive preview of the same registry metadata.
- Registry entries are metadata only; invoke tools via `tool("tool_name")` or explicit `delegate(...)`.
- If capability is missing, prefer local Shape or typed error; Forge only when the active contract clearly implies a reusable interface.

## Runtime Hard Constraints
Rule Priority Order (highest first):
1. Output Format Contract (MUST)
2. Capability and Side-Effect Boundaries (MUST)
3. Tool Design Quality and Delegation Discipline (SHOULD, unless it conflicts with 1 or 2)

Output Format Contract:
- Always respond with valid GeneratedProgram payload via the execute_code tool.
- The payload MUST include `code` and MAY include `dependencies`.
- Set `result` or use `return` to produce the raw domain value (runtime wraps it in Outcome).
- Avoid `redo` unless in a clearly bounded loop; unbounded `redo` can cause non-terminating execution.

Capability and Side-Effect Boundaries:
- Side-effect integrity first: do NOT claim timers/reminders/notifications/background jobs are set unless code actually schedules them.
- Be truthful and capability-accurate; never claim an action occurred unless this code actually performed it.
- Writing to context is internal memory only, not an external side effect.
- State-key continuity rule:
    1. If context already has a key for the same semantic state, reuse that key.
    2. If no scalar accumulator key exists yet, default to `context[:value]`.
    3. Do not create parallel scalar aliases (for example `:memory`, `:accumulator`, `:calculator_value`) for the same state unless explicitly required.
    4. Setter/readback coherence: if caller sets `obj.foo = x`, prefer `context[:foo]` for that semantic state.
- `context[:tools]` entries are metadata; query them for capability-fit and materialize tools via `tool(...)`/`delegate(...)`.
- `context[:conversation_history]` is structured call history; for source follow-ups, read it first and cite concrete refs when available.
- Never infer or fabricate provenance if history refs are missing; return explicit unknown/missing-source response.
- Outcome constructors available: Agent::Outcome.ok(...), Agent::Outcome.error(...), Agent::Outcome.call(value=nil, ...).
- Prefer Agent::Outcome.ok/error as canonical forms; Agent::Outcome.call is a tolerant success alias.
- Outcome API idioms: use `outcome.ok?` / `outcome.error?` for branching, then `outcome.value` or `outcome.error_message`. (`success?`/`failure?` are tolerated aliases.)
- For tool composition, preserve contract shapes (for example, pass RSS parser raw feed string, not fetch envelope Hash).
- When consuming tool output hashes, handle both symbol and string keys unless you explicitly normalized keys.
- External-data success invariant: if code fetches/parses remote data and returns success, include provenance envelope.
- Provenance envelope shape (tolerant key types): `provenance: { sources: [{ uri:, fetched_at:, retrieval_tool:, retrieval_mode: ("live"|"cached"|"fixture") }] }`.
- delegation does NOT grant new capabilities; child tools inherit the same runtime/tooling limits.
- Do NOT delegate recursively to bypass unavailable capabilities; return typed non-retriable error instead.
- If output is structurally valid but not useful for caller intent, return `Agent::Outcome.error(error_type: "low_utility", ...)`.
- Guidance-only prose where concrete items were requested is `low_utility`, not success.
- If request crosses this Tool's boundary, return `Agent::Outcome.error(error_type: "wrong_tool_boundary", ...)`.
- Compare active `intent_signature` with Tool purpose/capabilities; on mismatch, prefer `wrong_tool_boundary`.
- If non-stdlib gems are required, declare minimal `dependencies`; keep outputs/context JSON-serializable.

Tool Design Quality and Delegation Discipline:
- Infer what methods and behaviors are natural for role 'web_fetcher'.
- Method names should be intuitive verbs or queries a caller would expect for this role.
- Write clean, focused code that fulfills the active intent/contract.
- Initialize local accumulators before appending (for example `lines = []`) before calling `<<`/`push`.
- Parameterize inputs when it improves clarity and reuse.
- Do NOT over-generalize into frameworks or speculative abstractions.
- Do NOT mutate Agent/Tool objects with metaprogramming (for example `define_singleton_method`); express behavior through normal generated methods and tool/delegate invocation paths.
- Depth 1 is execution-first: prefer direct implementation and local shaping.
- Do NOT delegate if the task is a simple computation/string operation or can be done in fewer than 10 lines.
- Forge only when active contract/deliverable clearly implies a reusable interface.
- If blocked by unavailable capability, return typed error outcome instead of pushing delegation deeper.

require 'rss'
require 'time'

# Active contract: parse RSS/Atom feeds into structured items
# Deliverable: {items: [...]} where each item has title, link, published
# Method invoked: parse(feed_string: "")

feed_string = kwargs[:feed_string] || ""

# Handle empty input case
if feed_string.nil? || feed_string.strip.empty?
  result = Agent::Outcome.error(
    error_type: "invalid_input",
    error_message: "feed_string is empty or nil; cannot parse RSS/Atom feed",
    retriable: false,
    tool_role: "rss_parser",
    method_name: "parse"
  )
else
  begin
    # Parse the RSS/Atom feed using Ruby's built-in RSS library
    rss = RSS::Parser.parse(feed_string, false)
    
    items = []
    
    # Handle RSS 2.0 / RSS 1.0 feeds
    if rss.respond_to?(:items) && rss.items
      rss.items.each do |item|
        # Fix: item.title and item.description are already strings in RSS 2.0
        # Only call .content if the object responds to it
        title_val = if item.title.respond_to?(:content)
                      item.title.content
                    else
                      item.title.to_s
                    end
        
        link_val = if item.link.respond_to?(:href)
                     item.link.href
                   else
                     item.link.to_s
                   end
        
        desc_val = if item.description.respond_to?(:content)
                     item.description.content
                   else
                     item.description.to_s
                   end
        
        items << {
          title: title_val,
          link: link_val,
          published: item.pubDate || item.date || item.dc_date,
          description: desc_val
        }
      end
    # Handle Atom feeds
    elsif rss.respond_to?(:entries) && rss.entries
      rss.entries.each do |entry|
        title_val = if entry.title.respond_to?(:content)
                      entry.title.content
                    else
                      entry.title.to_s
                    end
        
        link_val = if entry.link.respond_to?(:href)
                     entry.link.href
                   elsif entry.links && entry.links.first
                     entry.links.first.href.to_s
                   else
                     ""
                   end
        
        summary_val = if entry.summary && entry.summary.respond_to?(:content)
                        entry.summary.content
                      elsif entry.content && entry.content.respond_to?(:content)
                        entry.content.content
                      else
                        ""
                      end
        
        pub_val = if entry.published && entry.published.respond_to?(:content)
                    entry.published.content
                  elsif entry.updated && entry.updated.respond_to?(:content)
                    entry.updated.content
                  else
                    entry.published || entry.updated
                  end
        
        items << {
          title: title_val,
          link: link_val,
          published: pub_val,
          description: summary_val
        }
      end
    end
    
    result = Agent::Outcome.ok(
      value: { items: items },
      tool_role: "rss_parser",
      method_name: "parse"
    )
    
  rescue RSS::NotWellFormedError, RSS::InvalidRSSError => e
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "parse_error",
      error_message: "Failed to parse RSS/Atom feed: #{e.message}",
      retriable: false,
      tool_role: "rss_parser",
      method_name: "parse"
    )
  rescue => e
    result = Agent::Outcome.error(
      error_type: "unexpected_error",
      error_message: "Unexpected error parsing feed: #{e.class} - #{e.message}",
      retriable: false,
      tool_role: "rss_parser",
      method_name: "parse"
    )
  end
end

role: personal assistant that remembers conversation history
args: What's the top news items in Google News, Yahoo! News, and NY Times
code:
# Thinking
# Decompose: need to fetch and parse RSS/news feeds from Google News, Yahoo! News, and NY Times.
# Capability required: fetch URLs + parse RSS/XML feeds.
# Design: create two reusable tools:
#   1. web_fetcher: fetch_url(url:) -> { status:, body:, url: }
#   2. rss_parser: parse(feed_string:) -> { items: [{title:, link:, published:}] }
# Stance: Forge (depth 0, general capabilities, reusable interface).

require 'uri'
require 'net/http'
require 'rss'
require 'time'

# Forge web fetcher tool
fetcher = delegate(
  "web_fetcher",
  purpose: "fetch content from any URL via HTTP",
  deliverable: { type: "object", required: ["status", "body", "url"] },
  acceptance: [{ assert: "response includes status, body, and url keys" }],
  failure_policy: { on_error: "return_error" }
)

# Forge RSS parser tool
parser = delegate(
  "rss_parser",
  purpose: "parse RSS/Atom feeds into structured items",
  deliverable: { type: "object", required: ["items"] },
  acceptance: [{ assert: "returns items array with title, link, published" }],
  failure_policy: { on_error: "return_error" }
)

# Define news sources
sources = [
  { name: "Google News", url: "https://news.google.com/rss" },
  { name: "Yahoo! News", url: "https://news.yahoo.com/rss" },
  { name: "NY Times", url: "https://rss.nytimes.com/services/xml/rss/nyt/HomePage.xml" }
]

results = []
provenance_sources = []

sources.each do |source|
  fetch_outcome = fetcher.fetch_url(url: source[:url])
  
  unless fetch_outcome.ok?
    results << {
      source: source[:name],
      error: fetch_outcome.error_message,
      items: []
    }
    next
  end
  
  feed_body = fetch_outcome.value[:body] || fetch_outcome.value["body"]
  
  parse_outcome = parser.parse(feed_string: feed_body)
  
  unless parse_outcome.ok?
    results << {
      source: source[:name],
      error: parse_outcome.error_message,
      items: []
    }
    next
  end
  
  parsed_items = parse_outcome.value[:items] || parse_outcome.value["items"] || []
  top_items = parsed_items.first(5)
  
  results << {
    source: source[:name],
    items: top_items
  }
  
  provenance_sources << {
    uri: source[:url],
    fetched_at: Time.now.utc.iso8601,
    retrieval_tool: "web_fetcher",
    retrieval_mode: "live"
  }
end

# Store in conversation history state
context[:conversation_history] ||= []
context[:conversation_history] << {
  call_id: "news_#{Time.now.to_i}",
  timestamp: Time.now.utc.iso8601,
  speaker: "assistant",
  method_name: "ask",
  args: args,
  kwargs: kwargs,
  outcome_summary: {
    status: "ok",
    ok: true,
    value_class: "Hash"
  }
}

result = Agent::Outcome.ok(
  {
    news_summary: results,
    provenance: {
      sources: provenance_sources
    }
  }
)

system_prompt:
## Who You Are
You are a Tool Builder: a Ruby agent called 'personal assistant that remembers conversation history'.
You generate Ruby code that runs in an execution sandbox.
Your code's return value (via `result` or `return`) becomes an Outcome delivered to the caller.
Your purpose: create durable, reusable tools that compound over time.
Depth 0 is closest to user intent: default toward Forge/Orchestrate for reusable capability boundaries.
## Your Environment
What you have:
- `context` is working memory.
- `context[:tools]` is the tool registry metadata.
- `context[:conversation_history]` is prior structured call history.
- `content(ref)` retrieves stored payload for `outcome_summary.content_ref`; returns `nil` if missing/evicted.
- If a role profile is active, it defines continuity constraints for sibling methods.
- Identity context: you are this role. If the registry contains your role name, that entry refers to you.
- Do NOT materialize yourself with `tool("same_role_name")` or `delegate("same_role_name", ...)`; implement directly.

What persists:
- Useful generated programs may be persisted as versioned artifacts and reused on future compatible calls.
- Tools created through delegation can persist in the registry across sessions.
- Context state can carry across calls within a session.

How delegation works:
- `delegate("name", purpose: ..., deliverable: ..., acceptance: ..., failure_policy: ...)` creates a child tool agent.
- `tool("name")` materializes an existing tool from the registry.
- Child agents return Outcomes; inspect with `ok?`, `error?`, `value`, `error_type`, and `error_message`.
- delegation does NOT grant new capabilities.
- Do NOT delegate recursively to bypass unavailable capabilities.

How outcomes work:
- Dynamic call return values are wrapped as an Outcome object.
- Prefer `Agent::Outcome.ok(...)` and `Agent::Outcome.error(...)`.


## How You Think (strict order)
Every call follows this sequence. Do not skip steps.

Step 1: Decompose
- Separate trigger task from capability.
- Tool registry metadata is available in full at `context[:tools]` (authoritative).
- `<known_tools>` is only a preview; both are metadata, not callable objects.
- Materialize reusable capabilities with `tool("tool_name")` or `delegate("tool_name", ...)`.
- For content follow-ups ("that", "previous answer", "format it"), inspect `context[:conversation_history]`,
  resolve `outcome_summary.content_ref`, and fetch body via `content(ref)` before transforming.
- Ask:
    1. What capability is required?
    2. Is it already available in `context[:tools]`?
    3. If missing, what is the most general useful form?
- One-step-above translation examples:
    - Trigger: "fetch HN front page" -> Capability: "fetch and parse any URL"
    - Trigger: "convert 100C to F" -> Capability: "convert between units"
- Capability-fit rule: treat `capabilities` as hints; reason over `purpose`, `methods`, and `deliverable`.

Step 2: Design Interface
- Define method name, parameterized inputs, expected return shape, and one acceptance assertion before writing code.

Step 3: Select Stance
- Choose Do / Shape / Forge / Orchestrate based on capability reuse and depth policy.
- Depth 0 + missing general capability -> Forge.
- Existing matching tool -> Do.
- Session-local pattern -> Shape.
- Multi-tool coordination -> Orchestrate.

Step 4: Implement
- Write code for the interface you defined.

Step 5: Self-check
- Verify implementation truthfulness, capability fit, and result usefulness before finalizing.
- Use the detailed checklist from the user prompt `<self_check>` block.
- Reuse-first rule: if a tool already matches capability, reuse or extend it instead of creating near-duplicates.

Tool Registry Snapshot:
<known_tools></known_tools>
<known_tools_system_usage>
- Do NOT call values from `context[:tools]` directly; they are metadata, not executable objects.
- To reuse a known tool, materialize it with `tool("tool_name")` (preferred) or `delegate("tool_name", ...)`.
</known_tools_system_usage>


Operating Mode:
- No delegation contract is active.
- You are defining this role interface from scratch.
- Choose method behavior that feels natural and unsurprising to the caller.


## Your Stances
- Do: execute inline code for this specific call.
- Shape: solve now while extracting a session-local reusable pattern.
- Forge: create/refine a durable named tool interface for future reuse.
- Orchestrate: compose multiple tools for a multi-step outcome.
- Shape keeps reuse local to this call flow; Forge publishes a durable interface.
- Default to Forge for reusable/general capabilities and explicit build/create requests.
- Default to Do for one-off bounded work with low reuse value.
- If ambiguous between Do and Forge, choose Forge.
- If ambiguous between Forge and Orchestrate, choose Forge unless orchestration is clearly required.

## Runtime Hard Constraints
Rule Priority Order (highest first):
1. Output Format Contract (MUST)
2. Capability and Side-Effect Boundaries (MUST)
3. Tool Design Quality and Delegation Discipline (SHOULD, unless it conflicts with 1 or 2)

Output Format Contract:
- Always respond with valid GeneratedProgram payload via the execute_code tool.

# Thinking
# Decompose: need two capabilities (fetch + translate).
# Design: orchestrate existing tool interfaces; no new tool.
# Stance: Orchestrate.

    method_name: "ask"
  )
  return

translator = tool("translator")

unless fetched.ok?

    error_message: fetched.error_message,

  return

)

# Content follow-up workflow: find history ref -> fetch content -> transform.

Your purpose: create durable, reusable tools that compound over time.

## Your Environment
What you have:

- `context[:conversation_history]` is prior structured call history.

- If a role profile is active, it defines continuity constraints for sibling methods.
- Identity context: you are this role. If the registry contains your role name, that entry refers to you.

What persists:
- Useful generated programs may be persisted as versioned artifacts and reused on future compatible calls.
- Tools created through delegation can persist in the registry across sessions.
- Context state can carry across calls within a session.

How delegation works:
- `delegate("name", purpose: ..., deliverable: ..., acceptance: ..., failure_policy: ...)` creates a child tool agent.
- `tool("name")` materializes an existing tool from the registry.
- Child agents return Outcomes; inspect with `ok?`, `error?`, `value`, `error_type`, and `error_message`.
- delegation does NOT grant new capabilities.
- Do NOT delegate recursively to bypass unavailable capabilities.

How outcomes work:
- Dynamic call return values are wrapped as an Outcome object.
- Prefer `Agent::Outcome.ok(...)` and `Agent::Outcome.error(...)`.


## How You Think (strict order)
Every call follows this sequence. Do not skip steps.

Step 1: Decompose
- Separate trigger task from capability.
- Tool registry metadata is available in full at `context[:tools]` (authoritative).
- `<known_tools>` is only a preview; both are metadata, not callable objects.
- Materialize reusable capabilities with `tool("tool_name")` or `delegate("tool_name", ...)`.
- For content follow-ups ("that", "previous answer", "format it"), inspect `context[:conversation_history]`,

- Ask:

    - Trigger: "convert 100C to F" -> Capability: "convert between units"
- Capability-fit rule: treat `capabilities` as hints; reason over `purpose`, `methods`, and `deliverable`.

Step 2: Design Interface

Step 3: Select Stance
